body_markdown:
*Welcome to our monthly market report, where we sum up the previous month’s activity in the collector car market with charts and key talking points using the data we gather every day.*


## Key Takeaways


- The[Hagerty Market Rating](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/how-the-hagerty-market-rating-works/) , which measures the status of the collector car market in terms of activity or “heat,” is up 0.14 from the previous month to 58.74. (The Market Rating measures the market as a whole, and any rating between 50 and 60 is still considered “flat market” territory.) This small increase is largely thanks to strong results from the 2026 Monterey auctions and general strength at the top end of the market.


- August’s numbers, and headlines, were dominated by[Monterey Car Week](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/2026-monterey-car-week-auctions-shatter-record-with-756m-in-sales/) . Sales totaled $755.6M across five auctions, beating 2022’s record year by an astonishing 60%. Results were driven by once-in-a-generation opportunities (ex-Clark Gable Duesenberg, Shelby Daytona Coupe) and low-volume hypercars.


- Global average sale price is up +31% year-over-year, while median sale price is up just +5%, further underscoring the discrepancy between the top of the market and the rest of it.


- YTD sales of $4.9B are up +42% year-over-year through August, which is the highest this number has been since January, another big month for live auctions featuring top-shelf consignments.


- The importance of newer cars is profound and growing. Last year the median model year offered at auction was 1991. One year later it is 1994. The volume share of vehicles built since 1990 has also increased from 53% to 56% year-over-year, and the value share from this era increased from 49% to 59%.


- The auction market is having a banner year, but gains continue to be concentrated in highly affluent pockets. The typical enthusiast with the typical car is operating under completely different dynamics, with values often falling in real terms.


[Greg Ingold](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/gregory-ingold/)

2. [2026 Ferrari Luce Tailor Made](https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/mo26/lots/r0150-2026-ferrari-luce-tailor-made/) sold for $40,000,000* at RM Sotheby’s Monterey
3. [1996 McLaren F1 GTR](https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/mo26/lots/r0170-1996-mclaren-f1-gtr/) sold for $34,655,000 at RM Sotheby’s Monterey

7. [1996 Ferrari F50](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1173405/1996-ferrari-f50/) sold for $14,575,000 at Mecum Monterey
8. [1995 Ferrari F50](https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/mo26/lots/r0050-1995-ferrari-f50/) sold for $12,105,000 at RM Sotheby’s Monterey
9. [2003 Ferrari Enzo](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1176628/2003-ferrari-enzo) sold for $12,100,000 at Mecum Monterey
10. [1985 Ferrari 288 GTO](https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/mo26/lots/r0066-1985-ferrari-288-gto/) sold for $11,555,000 at RM Sotheby’s Monterey
